evidence.claim: Travel along parts of the Baker-Copperfield route predates the scenic designation: emigrants used portions on their way to the Willamette Valley in the early 1840s.
evidence.quote: Early pioneers first traveled portions of this route on their way to the Willamette Valley in the early 1840s.

evidence.claim: Gold discoveries brought another wave of settlers in the 1860s, followed by people drawn to timber and farmland.
evidence.quote: Gold strikes on the southern side of the Wallowa Range brought another wave of settlers to the region in the 1860s. Later settlers were attracted by fertile valleys and abundant timber

evidence.claim: The modern corridor became a National Forest Scenic Byway in 1992, an Oregon State Scenic Byway in 1997 and an All-American Road in 2000.
evidence.quote: The Hells Canyon Scenic Byway was designated a National Forest Scenic Byway on April 19, 1992. It was later made an Oregon State Scenic Byway on February 19, 1997. The All-American Road designation was applied to the roadway on June 15, 2000.

evidence.quote: Wallowa Lake is a ribbon lake 1 mile (1.6 km) south of Joseph, Oregon, United States

evidence.claim: These ridges begin below the water and rise more than 900 feet above it.
evidence.quote: These moraines begin well below the water's surface and climb to over 900 ft (270 m) above the lake.

evidence.claim: The lake has appeared in geology textbooks as an example of water dammed by moraines.

flags: ODOT gives 218 miles and eight to ten hours; archived FHWA gives 218.4 miles and six hours. Used ODOT’s mileage and longer estimate. Its loop description connects two I-84 junctions rather than identifying the interstate as part of the scenic corridor.
Halfway’s name origin differs within its Wikipedia page: Pine and Jim Town versus Pine and Cornucopia. Omitted origin.
Omitted Coyote account because it appears only in ODOT’s retelling, without a cached Nez Perce source. Also omitted the unqualified six-million-year canyon account: ODOT says geologists believe.
Detailed Wallowa Lake geology has only Wikipedia support; no scientific primary page is cached.
ODOT lists recurring snow-closure dates, not a dated road-status bulletin. Practical checked date records cache review only.
Cache establishes designation sequence and earlier travel on parts of Route 86, but not builders or a construction narrative for Forest Road 39. Overlook moment kept short to avoid padding.
